A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Projected Coupled Diffusion research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across the reorganized appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original navigation simulations, PushT experiments, paired-image generation results, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds navigation environments, image-method comparisons, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The PCD framework is retained, but Eq. (9) changes the DPP cost from negative log cosine similarity to positive log, with epsilon greater than 1 instead of a small positive constant. Algorithm 4 corrects the projection clamp from max to min, adds a denominator safeguard, and includes dual residuals in stopping. These revise the specified procedure without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Navigation evaluation expands from Empty and Highways to include Conveyor, requiring directional corridor travel, and DropRegion, requiring stops at delivery locations. Both new environments are evaluated with two and four robots. PushT and the existing image-generation coverage, including two- and six-exemplar settings, are retained.

E2.justification: The image comparison expands beyond Stable Diffusion component variants to include SyncDiffusion and ControlNet-XS in Table 3 and appendix Tables 14–15. SyncDiffusion is adapted with the age-contrast coupling loss; ControlNet-XS supplies an attribute-conditioning reference. Navigation and PushT comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds SE-FID evaluation and protocols for the new image references and runtime profiling. Navigation projection settings change from 700 to 1000 maximum ADMM iterations and from 2e-5 to 3e-6 tolerance. Runtime profiling separately uses batches of 32 per robot and two to eight robots. These reported settings do not establish reruns of retained results.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds component-level runtime and robot-count scaling analyses. The existing image coupling-strength and noise-scale ablations gain SE-FID curves. Navigation and PushT ablations, obstacle-safety analysis, and latent-interpolation diagnostics are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Existing result-table standard deviations are retained. V2 additionally documents timing statistics over 100 diffusion steps from a single image-generation run and runtime means and standard deviations over 50 random navigation configurations. It does not report increased independent training runs or new seed controls.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for Conveyor and DropRegion, SE-FID scores, and measured runtime profiles. New image references achieve 48% XOR for SyncDiffusion and 8% for ControlNet-XS in Table 3, while PCD retains 96%. The detailed Empty, Highways, and PushT tables match v1; the main PushT table changes only rounding.

T1.justification: The preliminaries correct the score–energy gradient sign and restore the logarithm in the classifier-guidance likelihood gradient. Eq. (9) revises the DPP cost's mathematical definition and admissible epsilon, while Algorithm 4 corrects its projection expression. Existing derivations and method reductions remain; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: test-time coupling of pretrained diffusion models, projection-based hard constraints, no model retraining, and empirical effectiveness across navigation, manipulation, and image-pair generation. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly notes that existing projected-LMC convergence assumptions do not directly cover neural scores and frames external comparisons as demonstrations rather than state-of-the-art claims. It adds discussion of projection runtime bottlenecks, possible image-editing applications, and convergence risks from nonconvex obstacle projection. The earlier exemplar-alignment limitations and coupling–adherence tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies exemplar-generation prompts, detailed SyncDiffusion and ControlNet-XS adaptations and settings, single-GPU usage per run, and a PushT projection tolerance. It also adds timing documentation and a reproducibility statement describing supplementary code and planned model-weight release. The existing public code reference remains.

R1.justification: Related work gains reflected and constrained-domain diffusion references by Lou and Ermon and Fishman et al., plus hierarchical coupled diffusion by Hao et al. New references support ControlNet-XS, FID, and adaptive ADMM discussion. These extend the literature coverage without substantially changing PCD's research positioning.

P1.justification: Most narrative is retained with language polishing, merged related-work and setup/metric headings, and clearer cross-references. Appendix topics are reordered to follow navigation, manipulation, and image generation, with a dedicated runtime subsection. Reproducibility and language-model-use statements are added.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column main-text format with a single-column preprint layout and substantially rearranges displays. Figure 1 changes from a two-by-two arrangement to one row; Figure 4 gains baseline panels. New environment illustrations, runtime displays, and SE-FID panels accompany extensive relocation and resizing of retained figures and tables.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation with distinct navigation requirements and external image references, while Table 4 and Figure 11 replace the rough runtime estimate with measured costs. Corrections to the DPP formula and ADMM pseudocode, together with additional settings, improve technical clarity and reproducibility. These are useful incremental gains; the core findings remain stable, and the PDFs do not explain whether the revised method and solver specifications affected the retained experimental results.
